about: Corrections and documented changes to GridTilt's published facts. Hand-curated: one entry per actual change, with the value before and after, the source and its date, and when GridTilt reviewed it. Entries are added when a change ships; nothing is backfilled.

changes.field: Representative on-demand rental price, $/GPU/hr, all 10 tracked models
changes.source: Provider pricing pages and aggregator trackers (getdeploying.com, Silicon Data, aimultiple)
changes.scope: GPU Prices page (cards, index table, history anchors), Overview fleet-average gauge, the weekly brief
changes.rationale: The curated values were four months old. Neocloud list prices for Hopper and Blackwell parts firmed over the summer (Lambda, Together and RunPod Secure all list the H100 at $3.99) while the Silicon Data index and the recorder sat lower, so the blend moved up by less than the list prices did. GB200 and MI355X stay at June values because the only single-GPU on-demand prints found are thin or disputed.

short.label: H100 on-demand rental, neocloud blend
short.why: Four-month-old curated prices re-researched against provider pages and aggregators; Hopper and Blackwell list prices firmed over the summer.

changes.field: Basis of the June 2026 representative price
changes.before: $2.10/GPU-hr, which rested on DigitalOcean's 12-month reserved rate and a TensorWave contract rate rather than on-demand prints
changes.after: $3.05/GPU-hr on-demand (DigitalOcean $3.80, Cyfuture $3.04, getdeploying median $3.08). The June anchor stays in the series as recorded, so the chart shows a step that is mostly a change of basis, not a market move
changes.source: DigitalOcean GPU Droplet pricing (docs, last verified 2026-10-26)
changes.scope: GPU Prices page, MI325X card and history line
changes.rationale: The adversarial pass on the October refresh found that two of the three June prints were not on-demand rates. History anchors are append-only, so the correction is recorded here instead of rewriting June.

short.label: MI325X on-demand rental price
short.why: June's figure used a 12-month reserved rate and a contract rate; the on-demand prints run $3.04 to $3.80.

changes.field: Summer 2026 reserve margin and reference level
changes.before: MISO 13.4%, PJM 17.5%, ERCOT 15.8%, SPP 27.8%, each read against a single 15% reference, with a GridTilt "AI signal" beside them
changes.after: MISO 11.0% (NERC reference 8.1%), PJM 29.7% (18.6%), ERCOT 28.2% (13.75%), SPP 32.4% (19.0%), each against its own reference, with NERC's own risk rating
changes.scope: Overview grid headroom gauge, Power Map grid view, My Grid region card, region pages, weekly email
changes.rationale: None of the old figures matched NERC's assessment, and the single 15% reference and the AI signal were not NERC's.

short.label: MISO's summer 2026 reserve margin
short.why: The old figure did not match NERC's assessment, and GridTilt read it against a 15% line NERC does not use for MISO.

changes.before: Upcoming: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition expected December 15, 2026
changes.after: Published May 2026 (data through the end of 2025)
changes.source: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Queued Up: 2026 Edition
changes.scope: Catalyst calendar, Overview and landing previews
changes.rationale: The calendar listed an edition LBNL had already published as an upcoming December event.

short.label: the date of LBNL's 2026 Queued Up report

changes.after: 618 MW delivered, 75% of total capacity, as stated by Oracle; the source does not say what the figure measures
changes.rationale: The estimate was replaced by the operator's own disclosed figure.

changes.after: 192 TWh in 2024, 4.7% of US electricity; 521 to 843 TWh in 2030
changes.source: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, 2025 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report Update
changes.scope: Site search descriptions and FAQ, Analyze scenario baseline
changes.rationale: The old figure matched no published estimate; the scenario now starts from LBNL's.

short.label: US data center electricity use
short.source: LBNL 2025 data center energy report update

changes.field: Combined capex guide of the four largest US hyperscalers
changes.before: $340B, FY2025 guides as of the Q1 2026 earnings cycle
changes.after: $730B, 2026 guides as of the Q3 2026 earnings cycle (Microsoft ~$170B calendar 2026, Alphabet $195-205B, Meta $135-145B, Amazon ~$220B)
changes.source: Microsoft FY27 Q1 call, Alphabet Q3 2026 call, Meta Q3 2026 release, Amazon Q3 2026 release
changes.scope: /api/hyperscaler-capex and the operator pages for Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon
changes.rationale: The file had not moved since May 2026 and was two earnings cycles behind. Definitions differ across the four companies, so the total is directional.

changes.field: GPT-5.6 Sol list price per million tokens
changes.after: $4 input, $20 output, promotional price listed as available at least through November 21, 2026
changes.source: OpenAI API pricing page and API changelog (Aug 21, 2026 entry)
changes.scope: GPU Economics, the price of a token
changes.rationale: The registry was last checked on 2026-07-30 and missed the August cut; the same pass added the newer flagship and efficient tiers from all three labs.

changes.after: 250 MW fully operational critical IT (Applied Digital, Oct 2, 2026), operational
changes.scope: Compute Frontier, Power Map AI Clusters view, cluster metrics
changes.rationale: The developer stated an operational figure after the September Epoch calibration; the company statement replaces the estimate and the estimate flag comes off.

changes.before: 33 signed agreements, 30,939 MW with a disclosed size; newest announcement August 4, 2026
changes.after: 40 signed agreements, 35,837 MW with a disclosed size; newest announcement October 19, 2026
changes.source: Constellation, NextEra, Fervo, NiSource, New Era, TeraWulf and AEP releases
changes.scope: AI Power Deals, the brief's power agreements section, the Timeline and cluster deal links
changes.rationale: The registry's news check stopped on August 25, 2026. Nine agreements were added from the parties' own documents (Amazon and Google with Constellation, Google with Fervo and AEP, Microsoft with NiSource, New Era with Vistra, TeraWulf with Kentucky Power, Amazon with AEP and X-energy, and the NextEra and Google Duane Arnold restart, which had no row), and five existing rows gained dated notes on Palisades fuel loading, the DOE conditional loan commitments and FERC's Oklo ruling. No existing row's status changed; the 90-day firmness review of every row remains dated September 28, 2026.

short.label: Signed AI power agreements tracked
short.source: Party releases and 8-Ks, Aug to Oct 2026

changes.field: Figures in three March 2026 research posts
changes.before: The March 10 post and its card said 288 TWh and 6.4%; the March 2 post said 48 facilities and a 13.4% MISO margin; the March 4 PJM post said 250 GW, 4+ years and $270/MW-day with no sources
changes.after: 192 TWh in 2024 and 4.7% per LBNL; the March 2 post marked as a dated snapshot with MISO at 11.0% per NERC; the PJM post refreshed to $269.92 (2025/26) and $329.17 (2026/27) per PJM's auction reports, 220 GW in PJM's reopened queue and LBNL's 61-month median, each linked
changes.scope: Research index cards and three post bodies
changes.rationale: The September 28 and 29 corrections changed the site's figures but not the posts that first published them, so the Research page still showed retracted numbers. The posts now carry the corrected figures, their sources, and a dated note saying what changed.

short.label: Research posts' data center electricity use
short.why: The corrections of September 28 and 29 never reached the posts that first carried the old figures.

changes.field: Date RTO responses to FERC's large-load show-cause orders are due
changes.after: November 16, 2026, with answers due December 16, after a 90-day abeyance
changes.source: PJM notice to the Large Load Members Committee consultation
changes.scope: Queue tab regulatory row, the Timeline
changes.rationale: The row kept the original 60-day window in future tense ten weeks after it passed; the catalysts calendar already carried the November 16 date from PJM's notice. The Alphabet and Intersect row's source label was also corrected from 'Google press Dec 2024' to the December 22, 2025 announcement it already linked.

short.label: FERC large-load responses due
short.why: The original 60-day window was held in abeyance for 90 days; the row never caught up.
